Punitive

/PYOO-nih-tiv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Punitive means intended to punish — describing measures, fines, or actions designed to make a wrongdoer suffer a cost

Punitive means intended to punish. The rental contract hides punitive fees that charge triple the daily rate for every hour a car is returned late.

Worked Example

The trade commission slapped punitive tariffs on the importer, openly intending the fees to sting rather than merely cover costs.

The tariffs are punitive because their purpose is to punish — the sentence spells out that they were designed to sting, not just to recover expenses.

How Punitive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disciplinary

disciplinary: meant to enforce rules through consequences

retributive

retributive: designed to pay wrongdoing back with punishment

punishing

punishing: so harsh it works as a punishment

Antonyms

rehabilitative

rehabilitative: aimed at reforming rather than punishing

lenient

lenient: mild and merciful

How Strong Is It? — strict → punitive → draconian

strict vs. punitive

strict vs. punitive: A strict rule demands obedience, but a punitive rule is designed to make violators suffer a real cost.

draconian vs. punitive

draconian vs. punitive: Draconian is stronger than punitive, describing punishments so extreme they seem cruel for the offense.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pun-

Root — pun-: to punish (Latin punire, from poena, 'punishment')

Suffix — -itive

Suffix — -itive: adjective-forming; tending toward

Put it together

Put it together: Punitive builds directly on the Latin root pun- ('to punish'), the same root behind punish and impunity — anything punitive tends toward punishment.

Use the root in a new word: impunity

Use the root in a new word: impunity: Impunity means freedom from punishment: the vandals tagged the underpass with impunity until the city finally installed cameras.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / legal and policy

Punitive is the adjective for measures intended to punish — punitive damages, punitive tariffs, punitive fines. It describes the intent behind the measure, not the punishment itself: the specific fine or sentence a wrongdoer actually receives is the penalty, a related but distinct word in this unit.
